subject: Approval request: staggered A/B rollout with automated fallback for Novafin
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Li <jane.li@novafin.com>, ops+infra@acme-systems.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Approval request: staggered A/B rollout with automated fallback for Novafin

Hi Jane / Novafin infra team,

Thanks again for the productive call this week. To reduce risk during the next model swap (v2.3 -> v2.4) and to keep us within the committed uptime/latency SLOs, we9re proposing a controlled A/B (staggered) rollout with an automatic fallback and short-term version pinning as an SLA mitigation.

Summary of the plan (high level):
- Staged traffic shifts in 5% increments every 20 minutes (0% -> 5% -> 10% ... up to 50% for the first wave).
- Telemetry gating: If p95 latency for the new variant increases by >150ms vs baseline OR error rate increases by >0.8% over a 5-minute window, the system will automatically revert all traffic to the pinned stable version.
- Pinning: During the first 48 hours we keep the previous stable variant pinned and allow manual rollback only by the Redwood on-call owner (to avoid oscillations).
- Observability: streaming logs to your S3 (read-only) and our Console dashboards with alerting to both teams.

Attachments: draft auto-fallback policy and a short canary metrics runbook are attached for your review.

Ask: Can Novafin approve this rollout guardrail as an exception to the standard deployment flow so we can proceed on the timeline below? We9d like an authorization to apply the auto-fallback + pin for the next 72-hour window starting Tuesday (2027-05-04) morning PT.

If approved we will:
- Publish the canary run and post the mutual action plan in HubSpot (deal DF-4921).
- Schedule a 30-minute pre-deploy ops check with your infra team.
- Provide a 15-minute escalation contact window during the first 6 hours after initial traffic shift.

Please let me know any changes you need to the thresholds or timing; happy to adjust.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0117

Subject: Re: Approval request: staggered A/B rollout with automated fallback for Novafin

Karthik,

Thanks for the note and the clear plan. A couple of clarifying questions before we can sign off from our side:
1) "p95 +150ms" relative to which baseline window? Last 24 hours of production?
2) If the auto-fallback triggers, what9s the expected time to full revert and to re-open traffic?
3) We9d like confirmation that any on-the-fly pinning won9t affect our audit logs—need to preserve audit trail for our compliance team.

Procurement also asked whether this counts as a temporary SLA carve-out that needs to be captured in the change order for DF-4921. Please include any proposed wording.

Appreciate the attachments; I9ll review and get back with our infra owner (cc9d).

Best,
Jane
Jane Li
Head of Platform, Novafin
jane.li@novafin.com

Thanks, Jane. Quick answers inline and a small tightening of the proposal from our side.

- Baseline window: we9ll use the prior 7 days rolling baseline for p95 and median comparisons; the gating will compare current 5-minute windows to that baseline.
- Revert time: automated fallback is designed to complete within one token-cycle (typically < 60s) once the circuit breaker threshold is breached; practice has shown full traffic reversion visible in metrics within 60-120s depending on routing propagation.
- Audit logs: auto-fallback events are recorded as immutable audit entries and we will push the event payload to your audit bucket; we will include a short signed statement in the change order.

Slight tightening: reduce maximum first-wave exposure to 30% (steps: 0, 5, 10, 20, 30) to limit blast radius. If the first wave is healthy after 4 hours, we can continue wave 2 up to 60% in larger steps.

I9ll add the proposed carve-out language here for Proc: "During the controlled rollout window (2027-05-04 08:00 PT through 2027-05-06 08:00 PT) Redwood Inference may apply an automated canary fallback and temporary version pin to meet latency/upright commitments. This temporary measure is mutually agreed and will not be considered an SLA breach provided the auto-fallback is exercised according to the documented thresholds."

I9ve attached a tightened runbook as well. Ben, can you confirm on the credit/change-order ask?

Monica

Monica / Karthik / Jane,

I reviewed the tightened thresholds and the carve-out language Monica drafted. Approved with the following conditions:

1) This authorization is limited to the DF-4921 deployment window (2027-05-04 08:00 PT -> 2027-05-06 08:00 PT).
2) Redwood will record the event as a temporary carve-out and add a single one-time credit (0.5% of the month9s invoice) if a manual rollback is required within the window. Automated fallbacks do not incur credits.
3) Redwood ops must notify Novafin and the CS lead within 15 minutes of any triggered fallback and follow the runbook in the attached link.
4) Keep the previous variant pinned for at least 48 hours after the last rollback to avoid flapping.

Given those conditions, you have my authorization to proceed. Please publish the mutual action plan in HubSpot and send a calendar invite for the pre-deploy ops check.

Ben
